name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,351

clue.text: Charlie has hand split

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the left is one hand, as opposed to the right

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie has injured a hand, splitting it open.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft is the past participle of cleave, so a cleft thing has been divided or split apart.

clue.text: Cameron apparently thinks Syrian leaders are pussies

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the opening letter of each of the preceding words is taken

blocks.note: first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A jibe that David Cameron, the former British Prime Minister, considers Syria's rulers cowards.
explanation.walkthrough: Pussy here is the old word for a cat, not slang for a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Pussy is a familiar or childish term for a cat, so pussies are cats.

clue.text: Wait for old judge to cough up

blocks.note: to expect someone is to wait for them
O is the abbreviation for old
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Someone waits for an elderly judge to pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cough up looks like paying money, as the surface suggests, but here it means literally bringing up phlegm.
explanation.definitionFit: To expectorate is to bring up phlegm from the chest by coughing and spit it out.

clue.text: Fool keeps the Italian in the dark (mostly)

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside, so the fool encloses the Italian article

blocks.note: a twit is a silly person
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A fool keeps an Italian largely uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the dark looks like ignorance, but with mostly it describes dusk, when the light is nearly gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilit describes the dim half-light of dusk, a scene that is largely but not wholly dark.

clue.text: A mother and girl collaborate without hesitation for function

indicators.note: without means going lacking something, so the hesitation sound is taken out of the words before it
to collaborate is to work together, so the surviving letters are jointly worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A mother and her daughter work together smoothly, without hesitating, for some event.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from mother leaves MOTH; A, MOTH and GIRL then rearrange into LOGARITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: A logarithm is a mathematical function, the inverse of raising a base to a power.

clue.text: Biography with a twist at the end OK as rest from production

indicators.text: with a twist at the end
indicators.note: a twist at the end turns round just the closing pair of letters of the biography word

blocks.note: a life is a biography, as in Boswell's Life of Johnson
to OK something is to allow it

explanation.surface: A life story with a surprise ending is approved as a break from the presses.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland that lies fallow is left unsown for a season, resting so it can recover its fertility.

clue.text: Storm over British film star

indicators.note: in a down clue one word lies over another by covering it, so the storm surrounds the letter

blocks.note: a gale is a storm-force wind
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A tempest erupts over a British cinema celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was the Hollywood leading man of Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Pensioners here start to effervesce after mother's ruin

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken from effervesce
to ruin something is to wreck its form, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of effervesce
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly residents start fizzing after a drop of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin, which makes the surface about pensioners drinking; here ruin is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest home is a residential home where elderly or retired people live and are cared for.

clue.text: Wet spot around dance

indicators.note: around suggests being moved about, so the preceding letters are shifted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A damp patch has appeared near the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-step is a ballroom and country dance built on a sliding pattern of two steps.

clue.text: Poetry scam ruined the Authorised Version

indicators.note: something ruined is broken into pieces, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fraud involving verse has spoiled the King James Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised Version is the King James Bible, pointing the solver to scripture; read literally it is the officially approved text.
explanation.definitionFit: A master copy is the original, officially sanctioned text from which all other copies are made.

clue.text: Cut on the upper deck

blocks.note: first meaning: a joint of beef taken from the hindquarter
second meaning: a nautical term for being on or above the ship's main deck

explanation.surface: A passenger is left out of things, sitting up on the top deck of a bus or ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Topside is a lean cut of beef from the outer thigh, a common British roasting joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a butcher's joint of beef and a position above the waterline aboard ship.

clue.text: Pieces nameless receptacle stores

indicators.note: nameless means lacking a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped from the receptacle

blocks.note: a bin is a container for rubbish
stores and shops are synonyms

explanation.surface: Some items are kept in a container whose label has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the standard abbreviation for name, so BIN loses its N to become BI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops are chess pieces, the ones that move diagonally across the board.

clue.text: Alchemi can get upset by environmental issue

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the setter's own pseudonym, taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being troubled by a green concern.
explanation.walkthrough: Get reads as part of the phrase get upset, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate change, the warming of the planet, is the leading environmental problem of the age.

clue.text: Close river with diamonds in round the clock

indicators.note: in places the following words inside the river's name

blocks.note: nigh means near or close
the Tay is a Scottish river
and means along with
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A river nearby glitters with jewels all day long.
explanation.definitionFit: Working night and day means continuously, without stopping at any hour of the twenty-four.

clue.text: Is impressed by bald head after insult fades away

indicators.note: a mark impressed by a seal is pressed into the surface, so one piece is pushed into the other

blocks.note: diss is slang for insult
taken as written
a pate is the head, especially a bald crown

explanation.surface: Someone is struck by a bald man's head after an insult, and the effect wears off.
explanation.walkthrough: Is is not a link here but two letters taken literally, and it is they that wrap round the bald head, not the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dissipates disperses and vanishes gradually, like mist clearing.

clue.text: As golfer on fairway may have to negotiate the final details

definitions.text: As golfer on fairway may have to

blocks.clueFragment: As golfer on fairway may have to
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a golfer on the fairway may take an ... club and hit the ball ... of trouble
second meaning: to smooth away the remaining difficulties in an agreement

explanation.surface: A golfer approaching the green may need to settle a few last matters.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron is a type of golf club, used for fairway shots; read as a phrase the answer describes playing one out.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out is an idiom for resolving the small remaining problems, as in finalising a deal's terms.

clue.text: Unexpectedly find pleasant coat for soldier to wear

indicators.note: a garment that someone wears goes around them, so the coat wraps the soldier

blocks.note: to like something is to find it pleasant
mac is short for mackintosh, a raincoat
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is surprisingly pleased with a coat he is issued.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening like magic happens suddenly and inexplicably, as if by a conjuring trick.

clue.text: Manuals opener gets in

blocks.note: a key opens a lock
to board a bus or plane is to get in

explanation.surface: Someone opening a set of handbooks gets inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuals look like instruction books, but on an organ the manuals are the keyboards played by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ's manuals are its hand-played keyboards, as opposed to the pedalboard for the feet.

clue.text: There's no danger one has lines understood

definitions.note: a clause standing for the noun phrase: the signal that says there is no danger

blocks.note: a means one
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
something clear is understood

explanation.surface: An actor, reassured that the coast is safe, has learnt the script.
explanation.definitionFit: The all clear is the siren or signal announcing that a threat such as an air raid has passed.

clue.text: Cunning to admit reverence barely scratching the surface

indicators.note: admitting someone means letting them in, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: sly means crafty or cunning
to hallow is to revere or honour as holy

explanation.surface: A crafty person feigns respect while only skimming the surface of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something shallowly means doing it superficially, without going below the top layer.

clue.text: See 7
Tell skinny marines

blocks.note: the skinny is slang for inside information
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Someone passes word to the lean, fit soldiers of the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinny reads as an adjective for thin, but here it is the slang noun for information.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone is to tell them facts or give them news.

clue.text: Seaside attraction is able to accommodate strangely sober Northern Irish actor

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd fashion, so the following word is rearranged oddly
accommodating a guest means housing them, so the phrase for able holds the rest inside

blocks.note: a pier is a classic British seaside attraction
can means is able to
the letters of sober rearranged
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A seaside resort hosts a teetotal actor from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Irish reads as one phrase, but Northern supplies a letter and Irish belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierce Brosnan is an actor born in Ireland, best known for playing James Bond.

clue.text: Foundation of club as I specified

indicators.note: of here means made out of, so the letters come from within the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running from the end of club through as and I to the start of specified

explanation.surface: Someone sets out the founding principles of a club exactly as they stated.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support or starting point on which something rests, so a foundation.

clue.text: First person in Paris to grasp extravaganza could ultimately be green

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each of the two words is used
grasping something means closing around it, so the French pronoun encloses the letters

blocks.note: je is French for I, the first person
last letters of extravaganza and could

explanation.surface: A Parisian speaker takes hold of a lavish show that might turn out to be eco-friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is a shade of green named after the gemstone of that colour.

clue.text: Diggers ultimately prefer to be housed in drier quarter

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is used
something housed in a building sits inside it, so the letter goes within the drier

blocks.note: a towel is used to dry things
last letter of prefer
south is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Gardeners prefer to keep their tools somewhere dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowels are small hand tools used for digging in a garden.

clue.text: See 14
Welsh place's royalist leader returning to increase drama

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of royalist is kept
returning means going back the way you came, so the following phrase is read backwards

blocks.note: first letter of royalist
to add is to increase
Noh is a classical Japanese form of drama

explanation.surface: A Welsh town's monarchist leader comes back to add theatre to proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhondda is a valley and former coal-mining district in South Wales.

clue.text: Makes fun of way to cross American flags

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so the way spans the letter for American

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
A is a standard abbreviation for American
the yellow flag is a wild iris, so flags are irises

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the idea of crossing a road with American flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to ridicule a target through irony or exaggeration, which is making fun of it.

clue.text: Possibly over in Chile, by a mountain

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the run of letters is read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: letters running across the end of Chile, by, a and the start of mountain

explanation.surface: Someone guesses at a location: perhaps over in Chile, near a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe is an adverb meaning perhaps, the same sense as possibly.
